title: Screen Dimmer by Shardapps
shortDescription: Dim your Windows 11 desktop with a lightweight tray slider. Save quick levels, choose monitors and virtual desktops, and make it yours with six themes.
description:
Screen Dimmer by Shardapps is a lightweight, open-source software brightness controller for Windows 11. Make desktop output look darker, even when your monitor is already at its minimum hardware brightness. It works offline, without an account, ads or telemetry.

YOUR SCREEN, YOUR WAY
Open the mini panel with Alt+S. Drag the slider, tap a saved brightness level, or pause dimming. Pin the panel while adjusting several apps, then dismiss it with Escape. The panel clearly labels App brightness so you know you are adjusting software dimming.

USE IT FOR
â€¢ Late-night reading, coding, study and everyday desktop work.
â€¢ External monitors that still look too bright at their lowest hardware setting.
â€¢ Matching the perceived brightness of several monitors.
â€¢ Separate brightness for work and entertainment desktops in Windows Task View.
â€¢ An alternative software control when a hardware brightness adjustment is unavailable.

QUICK CONTROLS, PERSONAL SETTINGS
â€¢ Four editable quick brightness presets.
â€¢ All-display control, individual monitor selection and Identify screens.
â€¢ Optional profiles for detected Windows virtual desktops, including monitor overrides.
â€¢ Pin/unpin and pause/resume directly in the compact mini panel.
â€¢ Timed pauses of 5, 15, 30 or 60 minutes, with a visible countdown.
â€¢ Pearl, Midnight, Graphite, Ocean, Forest and Sunset themes, plus System.
â€¢ Smooth brightness, hover, focus and page transitions that respect Windows animation settings and high contrast.
â€¢ Optional warm tint, configurable opening shortcut and adjustment step.
â€¢ Optional Start with Windows and a separate Apply saved brightness setting. Enable both to resume saved dimming at sign-in.
â€¢ Immediate emergency restore: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12.

OPTIONAL KEYBOARD BRIGHTNESS CONTROLS
Native brightness-key input and Follow Windows brightness (compatibility) are separate opt-ins. Compatibility can help when Windows reports brightness changes but native sun-key events are unavailable. It also follows Windows-slider and automatic brightness changes. Show the App brightness panel on changes, or turn that feedback off. Support depends on what your keyboard, firmware and Windows expose; fallback global shortcuts remain available.

BUILT TO STAY LIGHT
Native C++20 and Win32, with no bundled browser runtime, driver or background service. Controls animate during changes, and the pause countdown refreshes only while visible. Preferences stay on your device. No screen recording or keystroke recording.

PUBLIC BETA
This beta includes the user-tested quick controls and keyboard compatibility updates. Source, documentation and reproducible issue reports: https://github.com/shardapps/screen.

WHAT SOFTWARE DIMMING MEANS
The app changes perceived brightness and colors, not the physical backlight, and does not promise battery savings or medical benefits. Uniform all-display levels use Windows desktop color processing. Different per-monitor levels use compatibility overlays with narrower full-screen coverage. HDR, protected video, remote sessions and exclusive full-screen games vary by environment. Sign-in, lock and UAC secure screens are outside the app's scope. The 8% app-brightness floor and emergency shortcut support recovery.

Windows 11 desktop app. x64 and ARM64 packages.

certificationNotes: Native C++20 Win32 Windows 11 utility; x64 and ARM64 packages. No account or test credentials required. Starts paused by default; drag the slider to enable dimming. Alt+S opens the compact panel; settings has Displays, Appearance, Preferences, Desktops and Keyboard. runFullTrust is for the normal desktop process, global shortcuts, click-through overlays and Windows Magnification full-desktop color processing. No elevation, driver, service, screen recording, keyboard hook, code injection or secure-desktop access. StartupTask and saved-dimming resume remain separate explicit opt-ins. Native HID brightness usage listening and Windows power-setting brightness notifications are separate off-by-default input modes; neither records typing or suppresses hardware handling. Compatibility follows logical level changes, including Windows-slider/automatic changes, and does not guarantee firmware/Fn delivery. Emergency restore Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12 restores displays, pauses and disables compatibility following. Uniform all-display levels use desktop color processing; differing per-monitor levels or unavailable/busy color processing use overlays. Virtual desktop detection uses local Explorer registry notifications and public desktop-manager fallback; no private shell interfaces or transmitted metadata. Pinning never opens a panel during quiet startup; passive feedback still dismisses. Quit from the tray menu restores desktop output. Public beta 1.3.1 includes user-tested 1.3.0 quick controls, reduced redundant native updates and a refreshed icon. Automated x64 behavior, startup, pause/preset persistence, resources, package/install/upgrade/uninstall and security checks accompany the release; physical ARM64/HDR/exclusive-fullscreen coverage is not claimed.
